ruling: (1) Chained task calls are Huey enqueues; a chained task's run failure is its own to report. The caller owns only the handoff: if enqueueing the next task fails, the caller writes an ERROR SystemLog `<next_task>_enqueue_failed` (error + traceback, on its own task_id) and keeps its own COMPLETED status. Applies to library_scan_task, the watcher (library_scan_files_task), library_enrichment_task and ingestion_task. (2) The watcher and ingestion_task write started / completed / failed SystemLogs like their peers. (3) Failed-run SystemLogs carry a traceback: library_scan_task and _error_boundary.task_failure_telemetry (artist matching, identity matching, embedding, normalize backfill, hash backfill).
rationale: Lance, 2026-09-29, after the AUD-021/025 gate-0 inventory showed enqueue failures were handled three different ways (flipping a successful scan/watcher run to FAILED, escaping unrecorded from library enrichment, silently swallowed by ingestion) and two tasks left no SystemLog trail. Implemented by PR #114, squash-merged to master as d89faf7 on 2026-09-29. Only the SqliteHuey storage error (sqlite3.Error) counts as a failed handoff; any other exception from the enqueue call is a defect and propagates.

ruling: RetroStation's background work is a command pipeline and is documented as one. A Huey message is a command to one named consumer that carries a scope (an id, or nothing). The work items live in status columns, which form the hand-off contract: broadcast_artists/track_identities.match_status (+ reason_code DEFERRED_RETRY), library_files.audio_hash IS NULL, library_files.enrichment_status, artists/works/recordings.needs_enhancement, stream_cues absence (stream_cue_work.NEEDS_ANALYSIS), library_folder_staged_hashes. Periodic tasks reconcile what a lost or failed command left behind. class.EVENT = 0 in the event graph is the expected state, not a defect. The contract is written once, in ARCHITECTURE.md (repo root).
rationale: Lance ruled 2026-10-05 on the Session C open questions (audit/eda/report.md section 10), answer Q7: target shape (b), command pipeline named honestly. Event graph 2026-10-04 (audit/eda/report.md): 14/14 messages COMMAND, 0 EVENT, 0 QUERY, max fan-out 2, unchanged in shape since April (7 -> 12 -> 14). All seven judged modules coordinate through the columns above, and that is why duplicate delivery is harmless. No consumer exists that an announcement would serve that a named command does not already serve.

ruling: D15, tags only: a local catalog artist (origin local, no MBID) is linked only to an artist MBID its own present files are tagged with (tag values split on , ; /, at most 3 looked up, most files first), and only when MusicBrainz's name for it normalizes (normalize_artist) to the artist's normalized name. MusicBrainz's special-purpose artists (SPECIAL_PURPOSE_MBIDS, or a bracketed MusicBrainz name) stay local. There is no name search (deferred, D15b). link_local_artists_task does it; mb_enrichment_task queues it through enqueue_or_log just before its re-check hand-off. The link is in place: the same row takes the mbid, origin musicbrainz and MusicBrainz's name, sort name and disambiguation, and is marked enhanced; ids, normalized names, works and match rows are untouched, and identity matching reads the catalog artist's MBID. Every lookup stamps artists.mb_lookup_at / mb_lookup_outcome (linked, ambiguous, tag_mismatch, special_purpose, duplicate, no_evidence; migration 0037); an unlinked artist is looked up again only when a present file of it is indexed after that stamp. Any HTTP, database or payload failure leaves the artist due; 10 failed artists in a row (HTTP, database or payload failures) stop the run, and artists decided without a lookup neither count nor reset that. An MBID that another catalog artist already holds is never written: duplicate, skip and flag, no merge. The targeted re-check's wave also holds the names of artists linked after its watermark, and the broadcast names matched to them, so their undecided songs are re-scored. Artist matching's outcomes are unchanged because NormalizationStrategy's fuzzy pass excludes the artists the linker linked, even if release enrichment later confirms the same MBID; they still match by exact name, with the MBID as target.
rationale: Lance, 2026-10-07 (D15) and 2026-10-08 (scope: tags only; special-purpose artists stay local; the search path deferred; no new artist-matching candidates; linked names join the re-check wave). Spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-05-matching-revisit-design.md section 2 D15; plan-readiness review 2026-10-08-matching-revisit-d15-review.md. Dev DB 2026-10-08: 3,221 local artists, 1,394 with MBID-tagged files; the 1,725 untagged ones' files carry no recording or album-artist MBID, so a search link could not change a song match. A merge was rejected: grouping re-creates a local artist from each file's normalized name. Without the fuzzy-pool exclusion about 125 broadcast artists would newly auto-match, many wrongly, and D2 would freeze them.

ruling: The event-graph analyzer's task envelope gains `context`. A task whose body has a `with` item calling a function resolved to a @contextmanager def (contextlib.contextmanager, bare name or attribute) whose body contains a try with at least one handler (nested defs not counted) has envelope `context`: that context manager catches the task's failures, as backend/tasks/stream_cue_tasks.py `reported_failures` does for the three cue tasks. The rule order is binding: (1) a with item calling a def named task_run -> task_run; (2) else task_failure_telemetry -> that; (3) else a catching @contextmanager def -> context; (4) else a try with a handler in the task body -> own; (5) else none. A @contextmanager without a try/handler (a timer) does not count and the task falls through to own / none. audit/eda/contract.md states the order; audit/eda/spec-gaps.jsonl GAP-01 is resolved by this ruling; audit/event-graph.baseline.json is refreshed (only the three cue tasks change, envelope none -> context). AUD-R011 and AUD-R012 (which tasks carry which lifecycle envelope) are unchanged.
rationale: Lance, 2026-10-09 ("let's do it"). GAP-01: the three cue tasks wrap their body in `with reported_failures(...)`, a catching @contextmanager, yet the analyzer reported envelope `none`, which misstated where their failures are caught. The event-graph analyzer tests pin the five cases (catching CM, timer CM, timer plus own try, task_run precedence, contextlib.contextmanager attribute form).

ruling: D16: a MusicBrainz outage defers songs, never fails a playlist. A transient MusicBrainz failure in song matching's Tier 1 Step B (search_recording) defers that song as needs_review with the new reason code MB_UNAVAILABLE, with no decision on partial evidence, and the playlist run carries on; permanent errors still fail the run. Song matching calls MusicBrainz only in Step B. services/recording_search.py RecordingSearch, built once per match_identities_for_playlist call (one playlist; never module state), translates a transient failure (HTTP 429 or 5xx after the client's own tenacity retries, httpx.TimeoutException, NetworkError, RemoteProtocolError) into the domain error MusicBrainzUnavailableError; any other error propagates and still fails the run. match_identities_for_playlist catches it around engine.resolve and writes the song needs_review with MB_UNAVAILABLE (tier unclassified, reason_detail 'MusicBrainz unavailable — deferred for retry at the next re-check'), through the guarded write (AUD-R018/R021; a refused write changes nothing); the old match rows are deleted and none is written. DEFERRED_RETRY stays the artist cascade's code. Step A's and Step C's results are never used for such a song, even a Step C auto-match (Lance, 2026-10-12), and the 56% floor never applies to it; a song that never reaches Step B is decided as usual. Cut-off: after 5 consecutive transient failures in one run (SONG_MB_FAILURE_CUTOFF) the run makes no more MusicBrainz calls and defers every remaining song that reaches Step B; any successful search, cached or live, resets the count. Every targeted re-check (rewind_wave) also rewinds every needs_review / MB_UNAVAILABLE song whatever its artist (BroadcastTrackIdentityRepository.rewind_mb_unavailable), so the fan-out re-matches them; the artist cascade's DEFERRED_RETRY songs keep artist matching's own existing reset (Lance, 2026-10-12), and decided songs that keep a reason, and artists, are untouched. Artist matching is unchanged.
rationale: Lance, 2026-10-12 (D16), answers: defer the song, do not fail the playlist; retry on every re-check; cut-off at 5; Q1 re-checks retry only the outage songs; Q2 a song whose Step B failed is deferred even if Step C alone would auto-match it; Q3 the worker log is enough for visibility. Controller ruling, 2026-10-12: a reason code of its own, MB_UNAVAILABLE, so the rewind selects exactly the outage songs; reason_code is TEXT (no migration) and the frontend renders an unknown code as 'Blocked · CODE' (no frontend change). Observed 2026-10-10: seven matching runs FAILED on a 503 from MusicBrainz's recording search, rolling back whole playlists (they recovered only when the 10:06 re-check re-queued exactly those seven). Spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-05-matching-revisit-design.md section 2 D16; review 2026-10-12-matching-revisit-d16-review.md. Accepted edges (controller): the cut-off is per run, so a fan-out pays again per playlist, at about 5.5 s per failed search (503: about 28 s per run, up to 42 min per 91-playlist fan-out) or 30 s per timeout (about 150 s per run, up to about 3.8 h of the single worker); intermittent 503s never trip the cut-off, and each failing song is deferred. Visibility (Q3): worker-log warnings (song_matching_mb_search_failed, song_matching_mb_cut_off) and the deferred cards, which the default queue hides; recovery waits for the next re-check (the MB pass after a library change, or Re-run Matching). The per-run and per-fan-out cost figures hold when the live searches fail consecutively; cached hits reset the count, so with interleaved cached answers the cut-off may not trip and the cost scales with the number of live searches (final review M1, 2026-10-13).
supersedes: AUD-R022: the targeted re-check rewinds only the wave's undecided songs (it now also rewinds every MB_UNAVAILABLE song, whatever the wave)

ruling: Rejected songs are parked and re-checked. Reject and Unmatch (identity_resolution_service.record_song_rejection) set the song to manual_rejected with reason USER_UNMATCHED (no reason detail, no tier), add the rejected file(s) to rejected_file_ids and delete its match rows; POST /identities/{id}/resolve answers match_status manual_rejected. Reject is allowed from auto_matched and manual_matched (their matched files) and from pending and needs_review (the shown suggestion, required); Unmatch only from auto_matched and manual_matched; every other status answers 409, including Unmatch of an auto_rejected or manual_rejected song and a second Reject of a parked song. Every matching re-check (the Re-run Matching button and the watcher's targeted re-check) rewinds manual_rejected SONGS together with needs_review and auto_rejected ones (SONG_UNDECIDED_STATUSES) to pending, tier and reason cleared, rejected_file_ids kept, so identity matching re-scores them without the rejected files and a new candidate is handled like any other song (it may auto-match, 56-94% goes to needs_review, nothing left is auto_rejected). A manually rejected ARTIST is never rewound (ARTIST_UNDECIDED_STATUSES stays needs_review and auto_rejected), and the artist MANUAL_REJECTED cascade still protects manual_matched and manual_rejected children. The 140 legacy manual_rejected songs need no migration: the first re-check rewinds them. The Resolution Center queue lists an artist only while it or one of its songs is pending or needs_review, so an artist whose only open songs are parked drops off the list until a re-check finds a candidate. A matched artist whose songs are only auto_rejected / manual_rejected (plus matched ones) is never in the main Resolution Center list, but is listed behind "Show N artists with no likely match" and counted in unlikely_total (2026-10-17, R7); the queue's likely rule no longer counts a song-level USER_UNMATCHED (it keeps LIBRARY_FILE_REMOVED and an artist-level USER_UNMATCHED). The song panel files needs_review without a score (except LIBRARY_FILE_REMOVED), auto_rejected, manual_rejected and unscored songs under a collapsed 'No likely match' section, with a 'Rejected by you' chip on manual_rejected songs; Resolved holds matched songs only.
rationale: Lance, 2026-10-13 (R1-R6). R1: manual_rejected and USER_UNMATCHED mean the same thing, the curator told the matcher its answer is wrong; such a song can still be matched and must always be re-checked. R2: a rejected song is re-checked on the next matching run (Re-run Matching or the watcher's re-check), not immediately; until then it is out of Needs Review. R3: on that run a new candidate that is not the rejected file is handled like any other song: it may auto-match; 56-94% goes to Needs Review; nothing left means auto_rejected. R4: a song with nothing to match drops out of the Resolution Center artist list until a re-match finds a candidate. R5: songs out of review are kept in one collapsed section headed 'No likely match'. R6: the parked state is the manual_rejected status (approach A), not a filtered needs_review. R7 (Lance, 2026-10-17, refines R4): an artist with nothing to review is never in the main list, but stays reachable behind 'Show N artists with no likely match'; a matched artist whose songs are only auto_rejected / manual_rejected (plus matched) is listed there. Spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-13-rejected-song-recheck-design.md sections 1-4. Dev DB 2026-10-13: 9 needs_review / USER_UNMATCHED songs, 140 legacy manual_rejected songs (no rejected files, never re-matched), 21,533 auto_rejected, 5 manual_rejected artists.
supersedes: AUD-R022 D2 (for songs): 'manual_matched, manual_rejected and auto_matched are never touched by a re-check' no longer holds for manual_rejected SONGS, which every re-check now rewinds to pending and re-scores without their rejected files; manual_matched and auto_matched songs and manually rejected artists are still never touched

AUD-R022 D8: 'existing manual_rejected songs stay frozen; unmatching one frees it' - Unmatch of a manual_rejected or auto_rejected song is now 409, and Reject and Unmatch park the song as manual_rejected / USER_UNMATCHED instead of returning it to needs_review

ruling: A matching run reports itself as one progress row. Every re-check (rematch_undecided_task) with playlists to queue opens one RUNNING progress_tracking row of task_type matching, after its rewind is committed and before its own matching_recheck row completes, with progress_data {processed: 0, total: pending artists + pending songs, stages_left: playlists, stages_failed: 0}, and queues artist_matching_task(playlist_id, run_id). The run id travels in the matching messages: an artist stage hands off identity_matching_task(playlist_id, run_id). This is the one exception to AUD-R015's scope-only messages; run_id is optional (None for an upload's matching, and for messages queued before the change), and with no run id a stage reports nothing. An artist stage whose hand-off is queued is replaced by its identity stage; every other end of a stage finishes it (failed unless an identity stage succeeded), including a refused enqueue, an exception and a re-check that fails after opening the row (each stage it did not queue). The last stage closes the row COMPLETED, with warning matching_stages_failed when any stage failed; a stage that raises still writes its own FAILED row through task_failure_telemetry. Each stage counts the pending work once at its start, on its own autocommit connection with bounded statements (never its transactional connection), writes it at once, then refreshes with start count minus settled items at most every 2 s as the matching services tick a MatchingProgress observer once per settled item; it finishes with a fresh count, else the estimate, else unknown. total = max(total, processed + pending), processed = total - pending. Writes revive a row the /ws reaper failed and never touch a COMPLETED one; all of it is telemetry and never stops matching.
rationale: Lance, 2026-10-17: during a Re-run Matching the UI showed no progress bar and kept the Re-run button enabled, so a second press would rewind and repeat hours of work, and the queue never refreshed at the end; only the 2 s re-check wrote a RUNNING row. Lance chose option (a), the run id in the messages with outstanding stages counted, over (b), no message change with the run ending when nothing is pending, which a failed playlist would leave RUNNING until the reaper. Spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-17-matching-run-progress-design.md.
supersedes: AUD-R015 (for matching stages only): a Huey message carries only a scope; artist_matching_task and identity_matching_task now also carry an optional run id

ruling: Song matching skips a MusicBrainz recording search that cannot change the song. Tier 1 Step B (search_recording) keeps only PRESENT files with the broadcast artist's normalized name that carry a recording_mbid, and displaces Step A only with a strictly higher score; a file tagged with the artist MBID (artist_mbid or album_artist_mbid) is already Step A's candidate and scores the same wherever it is found. So before searching, ResolvedArtistMbidStrategy asks RecordingSearchReachRepository.has_file_beyond_artist_mbid(normalized_artist_name, artist_mbid), once per (name, MBID) per match_identities_for_playlist call, and makes no call when the answer is False: Step B then finds nothing, as the search would have. Outcomes are unchanged. Such a song counts as one that never reaches Step B under AUD-R028: during a MusicBrainz outage it is decided as usual from Steps A and C, not deferred as MB_UNAVAILABLE, and its skipped search neither counts towards nor resets the run's cut-off. Songs whose artist has such a file are searched and deferred exactly as AUD-R028 says. IdentityMatchingRepos.recording_search_reach is optional; None (tests that predate this ruling) searches for every song that reaches Step B.
rationale: Matching profile 2026-10-18: in a warm full Re-run Matching Step B ran 11,778 times and won 0 songs; only 86 resolved artists (316 undecided songs) have a file it could add. On the cold run of 2026-10-17 its 3,924 live searches took about 72 of the 105 minutes the song stages ran (1.1 s MusicBrainz cadence). Deferring a song Step B cannot help only postponed a result that MusicBrainz could not change; the next re-check would decide it the same way. Lance accepted it on 2026-10-18 (PR #165).
supersedes: AUD-R028 (in part): a song whose artist has no file Step B could add is no longer deferred as MB_UNAVAILABLE during an outage

ruling: The artist model (design v3.1 sections 6.1-6.2). An artist is one performer, identified by its MBID, or by its local id when it has none; two acts may share a name. An artist's names come only from MusicBrainz names, MusicBrainz aliases and tag spellings, never from a log spelling, which lives only in log-name links (C43). Credits (ordered artists, joining words, main or featured) sit on performances (C44). Performances are a new table, each with its own id, its work, its recording MBID (unique where present), version and length; recordings stay as MusicBrainz metadata (C40). A work groups every performance of its composition by any act and is never split by a credit (M18, M21). Works are joined per section 6.2, including on a cached MusicBrainz work link (M29), through one merge path (C58) that pins every log line whose playing file would change, flags for Lance any change a pin cannot hold (C74), puts a hand-picked master first, and redirects merged-away work ids. song_masters stays each work's default copy: the work's default performance is the performance of its master file (C71).
